title: Write a `Consumer<Employee>` that prints employee details, then chain another consumer using `.andThen()`.
shortTitle: Write a Consumer<Employee> that prints details, then chain another consumer using andThen()
keyPoints: Consumer<T> performs a side-effect on an input and returns nothing
logDetails.andThen(sendAlert) runs both consumers on the same element, first then second
Unlike Function.andThen, no value passes between consumers: both act on the original input
If the first consumer throws, the second does not run (exception propagates)
Consumer chaining keeps forEach readable when multiple actions must happen per element
For independent effects that must each attempt regardless of failures, use try-catch per action

s1_definition.oneliner: logDetails.andThen(sendAlert) runs both consumers on the same element, first then second.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Consumer<T>** has a single `accept(T)` method performing a side-effect with no return value.
- **.andThen(after)** composes two consumers: both run on the same input, in sequence.
- **No value passes** between them; both act on the original input independently.
- If the **first throws**, the second does not run.
- Useful for sequencing multiple side-effects in a `forEach`.
s1_definition.analogy: For each new hire at the National Bank of India, Priya wants two things done: log an audit entry and send a welcome email. She glues the two actions with andThen so every employee gets both, in order.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  forEach element: Employee("Rajesh")
       │
       │  logAudit.accept(e)
       ▼
  AUDIT: Rajesh
       │
       │  sendWelcome.accept(e)    (andThen)
       ▼
  WELCOME: Rajesh

  Both act on the same original element.
  No value passes between them.
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
A Consumer performs a side-effect and returns nothing, and .andThen() composes two consumers so both run on the same element in sequence. Define each action as a named consumer, then compose with andThen for a clean forEach that logs an audit and sends a welcome per employee.

Unlike Function.andThen, no value passes between consumers; both act on the original input. If the first consumer throws, the second does not run. For independent effects that must all attempt, use try-catch per action.

At the National Bank of India, consumer chaining kept the onboarding forEach readable while performing audit logging and notification. Named consumers are testable in isolation, just like named predicates.

Remember one sentence: Consumer.andThen(other) runs both consumers on the same element in order, and stops on the first exception.
